messages.subject: likelihood in distance models
parts:
Hi to all the people using the package unmarked,

I just beggining to use this marvelous package, and I've found a
statistical-mathematical doubt. Is it possible to directly compare the
distance modesl by Royle and the one of the software DISTANCE through
AIC?
I know that it is neccesary that the log-likelihood estimation method
are the same, and I was looking into the literature, but I came to a
no clear conclusion, maybe because my low mathematical level (and
because I just arrive to home after being in the filed).

Can anyone help me? Many thanks

Pablo

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] likelihood in distance models
parts:
Hi Pablo,

The AIC values returned by unmarked and DISTANCE are not comparable because the likelihoods are different.

Richard

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: likelihood in distance models
parts:
hi Pablo,
 for us to help you diagnose the problem we would have to know exactly what are the two models being fitted.  It is most likely that you did something or another different in one of the implementations and that explains the difference.  Also, how do the density estimates compare to the average n per sample unit?
 
 Do you have covariates on abundance?  DISTANCE doesn't accommodate that. 
 
regards
andy

messages.author: 01f32dcbb5507b45
messages.subject: Re: likelihood in distance models
parts:
Ok,

let see the build of the models. The DISTANCE model is the default
one, being 698.98 the estimated surface (i.e. the area of the region)
and 16703 meters is the length of the counting census. Then there is
only the distance of the observer to red deers.

In the case of distsamp, I've build models using each link (i.e.
hazard, exp, etc), and selected the best one using AIC. The best one
in this case is the hazard. The code for R was as follows:

db<-c(0,21,41,61,81,101,121,141,161,181,200)
ciervo<-
unmarkedFrameDS(y=marina,siteCovs=NULL,dist.breaks=db,tlength=16703,survey="line",unitsIn="m")
Densidad<-distsamp(~1
~1,data=ciervo,keyfun="hazard",output="density",unitsOut="ha")

There are no covariates in the analyses as you can see. I think it is
difficult (or not even possible) to change the link function in
DISTANCE.

Many thanks again

Pablo

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: likelihood in distance models
parts:
I think you need to compare the estimate from distsamp() that uses exactly the same distance function as DISTANCE.  If those are not close then there could be some other inconsistency that we could address.
andy

Pablo,
 I may have misunderstood your email. Are you saying the estimates of density are "more than two times higher" or the AIC values are more than two times higher?
 
 As Richard said, you cannot compare AIC values so it is ok to expect a difference there.
 
 If the density estimates are very different then you have some inconsistency with the model between the two platforms or else an error in one or the other.
regards
andy
